vulnerabilities: Asymmetric dependence on China — heavy reliance on Chinese markets for hydrocarbon sales and Chinese suppliers for microelectronics and industrial machinery reduces Russia's diplomatic and economic manoeuvring room versus core Chinese interests

Black Sea and Baltic Sea naval bottlenecks — warm-water access requires transit through the Turkish Straits (Black Sea) or Danish Straits/NATO-dominated waters (Baltic), limiting free fleet deployment or reinforcement during conflict
Demographic decline compounded by wartime losses and brain drain, creating long-term shortages of specialised labour outside the defence sector

Western technology sanctions strain — historical reliance on Western oilfield-services technology, aviation parts, and specialised software has raised maintenance costs and operational inefficiency in civil aviation and deep-sea energy extraction
Extended northern and Far Eastern border-security burden across thousands of sparsely populated miles, requiring large standing security forces away from primary operational zones
strengths: World's largest nuclear arsenal alongside hypersonic strike capability (Avangard glide vehicles) across a complete triad of road-mobile ICBMs, SSBNs, and strategic bombers
Resource autonomy — full domestic self-sufficiency in hydrocarbons, agricultural output, and critical industrial metals
Sole physical/legal authority over the Northern Sea Route, backed by the world's only nuclear-icebreaker fleet
Defence-industrial scalability in land-warfare systems — high-volume artillery, armour, EW, and tactical-drone production under war-footing mobilisation
Diplomatic leverage via energy and defence exports to the Global South (arms sales, Rosatom nuclear-plant construction, discounted crude) to India, African states, and Middle Eastern buyers
